request: client contacts can be invited to an organization, raise and receive requests, and see nothing else
note: spec-slice --profile sharded produced 0 shards and assigned every criterion S-01..S-58 to the judge; all criteria below were answered by this pass directly. Currency was judged against the state the spec was written on (run baseRef de9c5f916fa328734ed5f8f9c77023e8720e35e8), because this branch already carries the spec's own implementation.

findings.claim: the shipping reassign route can act on a request carrying this spec's new addressee kind, and no rule in the bundle says what it does with one

witness.detail: `POST /api/organizations/{orgId}/requests/{requestId}/reassign` ships today: apps/api/src/requests/requests.controller.ts:167 (`@RequireCapability('ViewAllRequests')`), and apps/api/src/requests/requests.service.ts:807-811 writes `assigneeKind` and `assigneeMembershipId` on the locked row and touches no client column. It appears in no row of the Routes table (contracts:35-54). `grep -n "eassign" specs/requests/03-client-participants*.md` returns only REQ-03-035 (:332), REQ-03-036's Decided (:343), contracts edge case 5 (:557) and Known Gaps (:396) — none of which states what the route answers, or writes, when the request it locks is addressed to a client. Meanwhile REQ-03-035 (:332) requires a reassignment to write one outbox row per recipient and REQ-03-036's Decided (:343) reasons about the incoming and outgoing addressee of one, so reassignment is a live event of this feature; and the Data Model (contracts:293) says `assigneeClientMembershipId` is 'Required while `assigneeKind` is `client`, null otherwise'.

findings.suggestedFix: add one rule (and a Routes row) saying what the reassign route does with a client-addressed request — refuse it with a named status and message, or state that it moves the request to a member addressee and clears `assigneeClientMembershipId` in the same transaction — and say who the reassignment notifies when the outgoing addressee is a contact.

findings.claim: the unconditional invariant that no account holds both principals has a live violator the spec neither fixes, carves out nor scopes out

witness.detail: Invariant 1 (:378): 'An account never holds an active `Membership` and an active `ClientMembership` at once.' REQ-03-002's table (:76) makes the pair 'removed staff row + active client row' a declared, sign-in-able state. `POST /api/organizations/{orgId}/members/{memberId}/restore` (apps/api/src/members/members.controller.ts:59) sets exactly such a `Membership` back to `status: 'active'` at apps/api/src/members/members.service.ts:248-251 after checking only `can(caller.role,'delete-restore')` (:233) and `target.status !== 'removed'` (:244); it reads no `ClientMembership`. That is a third writer, against REQ-03-002's justification for the `active | active` cell at :74 — 'REQ-03-014 refuses the accept ... REQ-03-042 refuses the invitation and the accept ... and no other writer creates either' — and against contracts:269, which names REQ-03-014 and REQ-03-042 as the two writes where the exclusion is enforced.

findings.suggestedFix: state what the member-restore route does when the account holds an active `ClientMembership` — a named refusal with its status and message, or an explicit carve-out — so the `active | active` cell REQ-03-002 calls unreachable stays unreachable.

findings.claim: for an account holding a removed contact row in another organization, the accept rule requires a second `ClientMembership` row that the table's own unique constraint forbids

witness.detail: contracts:244: 'none | accept | A valid token with no existing row writes an active `ClientMembership`', where contracts:250 defines `state` as 'the address's `ClientMembership` at the client the invitation or the removal names'. contracts:269 gives `accountId` as `String @unique`. REQ-03-013 (:143) refuses an invitation only for a row 'of another client **of the organization**'; REQ-03-014 (:153) refuses an accept only for an **active** `Membership` or `ClientMembership`. Reachable sequence: organization A invites, accepts and then removes a contact; organization B invites the same address (REQ-03-013 sees no row of B — passes), the account accepts (REQ-03-014 sees no *active* row — passes), and the accept lands on the `none | accept` row for B's client. Writing the row violates `accountId @unique`; the alternative branch of REQ-03-012 (:138) — 'or return the account's existing row to `active`' — rebinds organization A's row to organization B's client, which REQ-03-013's Decided (:147) forbids for the same-organization case for exactly that reason. Out of Scope (:386) names 'a contact belonging to ... more than one organization' but states no refusal, status or message for it.

findings.suggestedFix: widen REQ-03-014's accept-time test to any `ClientMembership` of another organization whatever its status (409 `CLIENT_USER_MESSAGES.principalConflict`), or state the answer this accept gives, and say which of REQ-03-012's two branches applies when the existing row belongs to another organization.

findings.claim: the new picker route is gated on a role-keyed capability whose answer for the stored role value `member` is not stated, and the repository's two capability helpers disagree about it

witness.detail: contracts:42 gates the new route on `create-request`. The legacy-role paragraph (contracts:20-24) answers the stored value `member` for `manage-clients` and `view-clients` only — 'A membership carrying it holds neither `manage-clients` nor `view-clients` ... so `member` is refused exactly as `user` is' — and `user` is *granted* `create-request`, so that sentence does not answer this route. The two helpers in live use disagree for `member`: `can('member','create-request')` is `false` (packages/validation/src/index.ts:763-765, `CAPABILITY_MATRIX[role]?.[capability] ?? false`, matrix keyed by admin|manager|user|viewer at :620), while `hasCapability('member','CreateRequest')` is `true` (packages/validation/src/roles.ts:27-29 maps `member → user`, :187-189 looks the capability up, and `user` holds `CreateRequest` at :193). Both are load-bearing for request routes today: apps/api/src/requests/requests.service.ts:323 gates create with `can`, apps/api/src/auth/capability.guard.ts:57 gates decorated routes with `hasCapability`. TC-03-INT-36 (cases:349-361) exercises `user`, `admin` and `viewer` only.

findings.suggestedFix: say in the contracts which answer a membership carrying the stored value `member` gets from the request-contacts route (and from the create route's `create-request` check), naming the helper that decides it, as the paragraph at contracts:20 already does for `manage-clients` and `view-clients`.

findings.claim: the only case covering REQ-03-042 cannot reach the accept-time refusal its steps ask for, because the invitation it would accept is refused at the write

witness.detail: cases:257-259: 'take an account holding an active `ClientMembership` and, as an admin, invite that same address to staff; then write a staff invitation for an address that is a client contact of another organization and have it accepted.' REQ-03-042 (:157) refuses a staff invitation that is 'written for, or accepted by, an account holding an active `ClientMembership` of **any** organization' with `409`, 'writing neither the invitation nor the `Membership`'. The second step's address is already an active contact, so the write is refused and there is no invitation to accept: both halves of the step land on the same invite-time refusal. The accept-time half — which REQ-03-042's Decided (:163-166) says exists because 'the account may acquire the client principal between the invitation and its acceptance' — is reachable only by writing the staff invitation while the address still holds no principal, letting it accept a client invitation, and only then accepting the staff one. No other case covers REQ-03-042 (cases:248 is its only Covers entry).

findings.suggestedFix: re-order that step — write the staff invitation before the address becomes a contact, have the account accept a client invitation, then accept the staff one — and amend the Expected Result to name the accept-time `409` separately from the invite-time one.

findings.claim: the request asks that client contacts 'raise and receive requests'; the bundle delivers receive and refuses raise

witness.detail: The request reads 'client contacts can be invited to an organization, raise and receive requests, and see nothing else'. REQ-03-027 (:274) answers a client principal `403` `CLIENT_USER_MESSAGES.clientCannotCreate` on the create route; Out of Scope (:384) records 'A client raising a request. REQ-03-027 refuses it; the thread carries anything urgent'; specs/requests/README.md:78 records the same decision at area level — 'Staff ask clients, not the reverse, this release ... Named out of scope rather than half-built.' The decision is written down twice with its reason, so this is reported rather than blocked; it is here so the person who wrote the request confirms the reading before a run is paid for.

findings.suggestedFix: no edit needed if the reading is right; if it is not, the missing half is a client-raised request with its own topic audience, route, addressee resolution and notification recipients.

findings.claim: the retry rule names a bound it never gives, and no requirement in the bundle ever fires a retry

witness.detail: contracts:375-381: 'a row is retried only from `failed` and only while `attempts` is below its bound'. No number is stated anywhere in the bundle, and no requirement drives a second attempt: REQ-03-037 (:346) calls the notifier once after the commit, REQ-03-041 (:368) keeps every read path independent of delivery, and Known Gaps (:398) leaves the drain to an adapter spec. Nothing is observable either way with the shipped notifier, which is why this is a note and not a blocker.

findings.suggestedFix: either give the bound, or say plainly that no row is retried in this release and that the retry constraints are what an adapter spec must honour.

findings.claim: the amended list response fixes `counts.waitingOnMe` for a client principal and says nothing about `counts.total`

witness.detail: contracts:188-191 states the response 'carries `requests` and `counts` and no `vacation` member' and defines `waitingOnMe` only. The shipping route computes `counts.total` over a membership-keyed scope — apps/api/src/requests/requests.service.ts:205-214, `{ requesterMembershipId: caller.membershipId }` OR `{ assigneeMembershipId: caller.membershipId }` — which resolves to zero rows for a principal that is neither. TC-03-INT-23 (cases:487) asserts `counts.waitingOnMe` and not `total`.

findings.suggestedFix: one clause saying `counts.total` is the count of the requests the client principal's own scope returns.

findings.claim: two new user-visible strings are described rather than given, so no case can assert either

witness.detail: contracts:527: '`client-contacts-empty-state` with a line saying what a contact is for'. contracts:531: 'the requests empty state, with copy that does not mention scopes or filters they do not have'. Neither names an export, and the Error Messages table (contracts:200-230) carries no row for either; the existing `REQUEST_MESSAGES.emptyMine` ('Nothing is waiting on you.', packages/validation/src/index.ts) would satisfy the second but is not named.

findings.suggestedFix: name the export and the exact text for the contacts empty state, and say whether the client's requests empty state reuses `REQUEST_MESSAGES.emptyMine`.

findings.claim: three edge cases have no case and no line saying they have none

witness.detail: Edge 4 (contracts:556, the client archived while a contact is signed in — TC-03-INT-06 archives before the invitation, never with a live session), edge 6 (contracts:558, the requester unassigned after raising), edge 14 (contracts:566, a recipient's principal removed before delivery, which no case asserts: with the shipped notifier every row is `skipped` for every recipient, so TC-03-INT-24 cannot tell the removal apart).

findings.suggestedFix: give each an observer, or one line naming the case that already covers it.

findings.claim: the lock is stated for a request's status write and for nothing else, including the row two writers of this spec share

witness.detail: Invariant 3 (:380) states the `FOR UPDATE` re-read for every write of a request's status. A `ClientMembership.status` is written by two paths this spec adds — the removal (REQ-03-006, :99) and the accept that returns a removed row to `active` (REQ-03-012, :136) — and neither says what is locked or re-read, nor that they cannot race.

findings.suggestedFix: one line: either the lock and what is re-read inside the transaction, or that the two writes cannot race in ordinary use and no lock is added.

criteriaNotes.S-01: Every named symbol exists at the baseline the spec was written on: SessionGuard, OrgScopeGuard, MailService as an abstract DI token (apps/api/src/mail/mail.service.ts:152), normalizeRole/hasCapability/ROLE_CAPABILITIES (roles.ts), can/CAPABILITY_MATRIX (index.ts:620,763), the e2e helpers signupOrg/latestInvitationToken/createBareAccount/inviteAndAcceptViaApi/assignProjectMembersViaApi, and apps/api/test/{clients,requests,session-revocation}.spec.ts.
criteriaNotes.S-02: Every quoted message matches its export character for character (AUTH_MESSAGES.deactivated/invalidCredentials, INVITE_MESSAGES.tokenInvalid, CLIENT_MESSAGES.clientArchived, the fourteen REQUEST_MESSAGES rows, REQUEST_TOPIC_MESSAGES.pickerEmpty).
criteriaNotes.S-03: Statuses match the shipping routes: create 201, messages 201, answer/grant/decline 200 (requests.controller.ts), POST /api/invitations 200 and accept 200 (invitations.controller.ts:21-39), GET /api/me 200-with-null (me.controller.ts:27).
criteriaNotes.S-04: Schema facts hold: Membership.accountId @unique, Invitation.role free-form String with no clientId, Request.assigneeKind with nullable assigneeMembershipId, RequestMessage.authorKind, RequestEvent.actorKind.
criteriaNotes.S-05: 'Today the code does X' claims verified: /api/me answers null for an account with no membership; the login membership check precedes the password compare (login.service.ts:34-41); nav-members is drawn unconditionally while every other row asks a capability (Sidebar.tsx:72-105); the two seeded client topics are Access (access, 10) and Other (question, 20) (request-topics.seed.ts:37-38); the list route answers 400 validation_error before it consults a capability (requests.service.ts:168-188).
criteriaNotes.S-06: Select and Toggle are exported by apps/web/src/ds.ts; SelectOption.label is React.ReactNode (1_DS for dev/components/forms/Select.d.ts:3), so the DS-gaps table's 'None' holds.
criteriaNotes.S-08: spec-lint ran clean on this bundle in this round (T0), which settles counts, coverage joins and cited paths.
criteriaNotes.S-28: TC-03-E2E-01..05 each reach something an API test cannot: mail-to-session journey, a nav row that must not be drawn, the shell's redirect after revocation, the modal's audience re-read, and the client's action controls. No existing e2e covers revocation-on-removal.
criteriaNotes.S-44: Tied to R5: the accept-time half of REQ-03-042 has no case that would fail if it were implemented backwards.
criteriaNotes.S-54: No external system: the shipped notifier makes no outbound call and the Access table records no credential.
